To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SET index, which is a composite of 106 genes positively and 59 genes negatively correlated with ER mRNA, predicts benefit from tamoxifen in patients with ER- positive breast cancer.

the SET index (a genomic index for sensitivity of endocrine therapy) is a prognostic factor for relapse and survival of ER-positive breast cancer patients treated with endocrine therapy, and it can be used to identify subsets of patients with ER-positive breast cancer who will benefit from endocrine treatment.
the SET index, a genomic index for endocrine sensitivity in breast cancer, is a better predictor of outcome with endocrine therapy than the estrogen receptor (ER)-mRNA expression.

the molecular basis of breast cancer.
the identification of genes and pathways involved in the development, maintenance, and progression of human breast cancer.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SET index, as reported by Symmans etal, is an excellent candidate for a new standard of care for the assessment of ER-positive breast cancer.

the ER status is a good predictor of hormone response in the metastatic setting, but it is a poor predictor in the early setting, and it is a poor negative predictor of hormone therapy in both settings.
the SET index, which is based on ER-positive breast cancer, may be a more powerful predictor of benefit from hormone therapy than the ER status alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ER expression is a necessary but not sufficient condition for endocrine therapy response.
the SET index predicts benefit from endocrine treatment but is not prognostic.
we are in a new era of biomarker development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the expression of ER itself is not a perfect predictor of benefit from endoxifen, and we need to find a way to improve on that.
the SET index, as a measure of ER activity, is a better predictor of benefit from endo-crine therapy than ER expression or PR expression alone.
the SET index can be used in the clinic as a tool to identify patients most likely to benefit from endocrine treatment.
